bugs: Unauthenticated DELETE /api/auth/token or GET /api/me without an `Accept: application/json` header returns 500 (RouteNotFoundException: Route [login] not defined). Authenticate middleware calls redirectTo() for non-JSON requests before the exception renderer runs, so shouldRenderJsonWhen does not help. A mobile client that leaves out the Accept header gets 500 instead of 401.

Array `email` input (email[]=x) gives 500: the throttle key callback does str($request->input('email')) before validation runs, which converts an array to a string (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:25-27).
antipatterns: app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:26 — ->trim() does nothing because the global TrimStrings middleware already trims input before throttle runs
tests/Feature/TokenAuthTest.php:175 — the end-to-end test asserts Hash::check on the stored password, which only tests the model's hashed cast, not this feature
tests/Feature/TokenAuthTest.php:121,151 — guest tests cover only JSON clients, so the 500 for plain requests goes unnoticed
tests/Feature/TokenAuthTest.php:77,89,99,111 — throttle setup loops don't check that the earlier attempts returned 401
strengths: Thin controllers: an invokable MeController and a resourceful store/destroy on TokenController
FormRequest with validated() access; generic 401 for both wrong email and wrong password, so it doesn't reveal which emails exist
Throttle key is the lowercased email plus IP, using a named RateLimiter and throttle middleware
Tests use describe blocks and a dataset with the `:field` description; they check the token name/owner, revoking only the current token, and expiry of the throttle window via travel()

bugs: Array `email` input (email[]=x) gives 500: str($request->input('email')) in the rate-limiter key runs before validation (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:25-26).
antipatterns: bootstrap/app.php:16 — still sends non-API guests to route('login'), which doesn't exist; harmless for this API but keeps a broken fallback
tests/Feature/TokenAuthTest.php:38 — inconsistent double quotes in str_replace("_", " ", ...); the validation-message check is a loose substring match
tests/Feature/TokenAuthTest.php:15-17 — a shared $this->user in beforeEach makes the tests rely on implicit fixture state
strengths: Uses redirectGuestsTo in bootstrap/app.php so unauthenticated API requests without an Accept header get a proper 401 JSON response instead of a 500 (the main difference from impl-1)
Tests cover plain non-JSON clients ($this->delete / $this->get) for the unauthenticated paths

Throttle tests check that every earlier attempt returned 401 and that a correct password is still blocked once the limit is reached; tests also cover case-insensitivity, separate counters per IP and per email, and expiry of the window
Same clean controller, FormRequest and named-limiter design; generic 401 message; token response contains only the plain-text token

v.rationale: The two implementations are almost the same: the same FormRequest, the same TokenController store/destroy, the same invokable MeController and the same named rate limiter keyed on lowercased email plus IP. Both test suites pass (impl-2: 20 tests, impl-1: 19). My probes found what separates them. In impl-1, an unauthenticated DELETE /api/auth/token or GET /api/me without `Accept: application/json` returns 500 (Route [login] not defined), because Authenticate builds the redirect URL before the JSON renderer runs. That breaks the requirement for correct status codes for every client. impl-2 fixed this with redirectGuestsTo and tested it with plain requests. Both return 500 when `email` is sent as an array, because the throttle key callback runs before validation. impl-1's tests are a little better organised (describe blocks), but they include a meaningless Hash::check assertion and a redundant trim() in the throttle key. impl-2 checks more in its throttle tests and covers non-JSON clients. impl-2 ranks first.
